title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: THE FIREHOUSE DINNER
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Mavis Greer, sixty-eight, of Canyon, Texas.
For forty years she climbed telephone poles. Retirement was the first thing that ever scared her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE KNOCK
segments.quote: I don't want to belong to any club that will accept me as a member.
segments.author: Groucho Marx
lines: In October, Fire Chief Earl Dobbs asked her to help with the firehouse Thanksgiving dinner.
Mavis laughed and quoted Groucho Marx:
I don't want to belong to any club that will accept me as a member.
Earl said, It's not a club. It's five old men and a turkey fryer.
She signed up that night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE OLD WAY
segments.quote: The most dangerous phrase in the language is, 'We've always done it this way.'
segments.author: Grace Hopper
lines: The dinner was on a Tuesday afternoon. Thirty-one people came last year.
Why Tuesday? Earl said, We've always done it this way.
She thought of Grace Hopper, the Navy admiral and computer pioneer:
The most dangerous phrase in the language is, We've always done it this way.
So she moved it to Saturday noon and hung flyers all over town.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE MEETINGS
segments.quote: Do nothing which is of no use.
segments.author: Miyamoto Musashi
lines: Then came the planning meetings. Three hours each, mostly about a grease fire in nineteen eighty-seven.
At the used bookstore, she found Miyamoto Musashi, an old Japanese swordsman:
Do nothing which is of no use.
Next Monday, she brought a kitchen timer. Thirty minutes, then pie.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE FRYER
segments.quote: There's absolutely no reason for being rushed along with the rush.
segments.author: Robert Frost
lines: Soon three hundred people had signed up. Mavis panicked and bought a giant fryer.
She tested it that day. The flames reached the basketball hoop.
Earl put it out and quoted the poet Robert Frost:
There's absolutely no reason for being rushed along with the rush.
So they slowed down. Earl taught her the safe way, one turkey at a time. Mavis kept both eyebrows.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE LIST
segments.quote: You have not lived today until you have done something for someone who can never repay you.
segments.author: Old saying
lines: The night before, Mavis frowned at the list. Who were all these people?
Earl said, Widowers. Truckers far from home. Folks who eat alone.
Her mother's recipe box held an old saying:
You have not lived today until you have done something for someone who can never repay you.
So at dawn, she picked up Mister Ochoa, ninety-one, who hadn't left his ranch since spring.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE DINNER
segments.author: Heraclitus
lines: On Saturday, three hundred and twelve people came.
And Earl, Mister We've Always Done It This Way, stayed till midnight washing every pot.
Mavis remembered Heraclitus, the ancient Greek thinker:
Character is destiny.
So she voted Earl next year's chair. He grumbled, then bought his own kitchen timer.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Show up. Question the old way. Cut the useless. Slow down. Give freely. Trust good character.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Show up. Question the old way. Cut the useless. Slow down. Give freely. Trust good character.
Me? I once fried a turkey. The fire department still sends me a Thanksgiving card.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
